requirements.summary: 2 GHz dual-core · 6 GB RAM · 25 GB disk · 8 GB USB
requirements.note: Canonical's desktop figures: a 2 GHz dual-core processor, 6 GB system memory and 25 GB of free disk, plus a USB port or DVD drive for the installer. The installation medium needs an 8 GB stick or larger.

page.description: Ubuntu editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: Canonical's newest release, on a nine-month clock: GNOME 51, Linux 7.3, an amd64v3 build and RISC-V desktop media. Pick Desktop or Server, then the architecture of the machine that will run it.
pros: The latest Ubuntu release: GNOME 51 and Linux 7.3, newer than the 26.04 LTS.
Desktop media for amd64, arm64, RISC-V and an amd64v3-optimised build.
Server images for amd64, arm64, ppc64el, s390x and RISC-V in the same release.
Nine months of free security and maintenance updates, until July 2027.
cons: Nine months only: production machines belong on 26.04.1 LTS, supported until April 2031.
The release images carry kernel 7.3.0-9.9, built from 7.3-rc6 because upstream 7.3 landed after GA.
Desktop wants 6 GB RAM and 25 GB of free disk; below that Canonical recommends Xubuntu or Lubuntu.
The erase-disk option takes the entire selected drive, and writing the stick erases it.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of Ubuntu 16.04 with the Unity desktop from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 26.10 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: Ubuntu 16.04 Unity desktop with Files, a terminal and LibreOffice open
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of Ubuntu 16.04 (Unity) · not 26.10, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: Two official paths: the Desktop and Server ISOs, written to an 8 GB or larger stick with Disks, Startup Disk Creator or dd. Writing erases the stick; the installer's erase-disk option erases the target disk. For five years of updates, use 26.04.1 LTS instead.

editions.name: Desktop
editions.description: The GNOME desktop Canonical ships, with the installer on the same ISO: try it live, then install or repartition.
editions.usbNote: 8 GB stick or larger. Disks (Restore Disk Image), Startup Disk Creator or dd; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Desktop amd64v3
editions.description: The same desktop built with x86-64-v3 (AVX2) instructions, for Intel and AMD processors new enough to run them.
editions.usbNote: 8 GB stick or larger. For x86-64-v3 CPUs only; older machines need the plain amd64 image.

editions.name: Server
editions.description: The same release without a desktop: the live server installer for machines that are administered over SSH or a console.
editions.usbNote: Bootable on amd64 and arm64. The ppc64el, s390x and RISC-V images target their own firmware and hypervisors, not a PC USB stick.
